captured_note: Ported from the lab's ARSSL scratch trainer (methods_step3/ARSSL/src/models/train_igpt_scratch.py), which defines its iGPT model inline rather than importing the image-gpt-pytorch submodule. So this is a self-contained re-implementation of lab code, the same treatment the six official methods received -- there is no third_party submodule for image_gpt.

paper.title: Generative Pretraining from Pixels (Image GPT)
paper.authors: Chen, Radford, Child, Wu, Jun, Luan, Sutskever

upstream_reference.note: Not imported or copied. The lab's inline model credits teddykoker/image-gpt (a PyTorch reproduction; the original openai/image-gpt is TensorFlow 1.x). The lab's inline IGPTSmall is the lab's own code and is what this port re-implements; the teddykoker repo is a docstring reference only.

encoder: encoder.pt is the representation side of the model: the token and position embeddings (token_embed, pos_embed), the transformer blocks (blocks), and the final norm (ln_f). The generative head (head) is excluded, so encoder.pt is the representation network.
linear_eval: Unlike the generative ports var and mar, iGPT's downstream representation is the model this port trains: IGPT.extract_features -- a middle transformer layer, mean-pooled. So linear_eval reads the trained encoder.pt and its number is a genuine, comparable linear probe (not a tokeniser probe). It also reads clusters.npy (written by step 1) to quantise images with the same colour space the model was trained on.
colour_quantisation: iGPT feeds the transformer discrete colour-cluster tokens. The lab used sklearn's MiniBatchKMeans; this port re-implements a deterministic Lloyd k-means in numpy (quantize.py). Two measured reasons: the lab's saved clusters are not in the capture, so exact clusters cannot be reproduced regardless; and keeping the dependency stack at torch/torchvision/numpy matches the self-contained methods and keeps the lock light. Colour quantisation is preprocessing, not the SSL representation.
rewritten_during_the_port: the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA (the lab wrapper reached CUDA through init_distributed_mode)
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch)
the training loop drops the upstream DDP (DistributedDataParallel) and torch.cuda.amp machinery so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged
the colour quantiser is a deterministic numpy k-means rather than sklearn's MiniBatchKMeans
DATA_ROOT is the dataset root; the pretrain stage reads its train/ subdirectory (unified data-root convention via adapterlib.dataset_split_dir).
